subject: Next steps: Aurelia Health isolated GPU onramp & ops checklist
messages:
From: Diego Fernández <diego@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hargrove <tom.hargrove@aurelia.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Aurelia onramp: notes + baseline ask

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick summary from our side and a handful of clear asks so we can map this into a pilot + SOW: 

Pain points you called out
- PHI processing: all inference requests for clinical triage must remain in a dedicated, customer-controlled network (VPC) and we need evidence of KMS audits for encryption at-rest.
- Peak latency variability: current infra shows p95 spikes >700ms during morning ramp, you want p95 under 250ms for triage flows.
- Cost predictability: CFO needs a committed monthly baseline with defined burst economics to avoid surprise bills.

Goals we agreed
- Baseline throughput: ~100 concurrent requests sustained (~30 tokens/request average)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms, aim for 200ms on final config
- Isolation: private pool (single-tenant) with VPC peering + strict egress controls
- Pilot: 2-week functional pilot followed by 90-day ramp to production

Proposed capacity & ops sketch (first draft)
- Baseline: 8 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs in an isolated pool (reserved)
- Burst: auto-burst to 24 GPUs for scheduled windows (06:00–10:00 PT) via reserved burst credits
- Runtime defaults: INT8 quantized variant for cost-sensitive endpoints, full fp16 for critical triage route
- Fallback policy: if isolation pool is saturated, route least-sensitive requests to hosted compatible model with rate-limited fallback

SLA targets
- Uptime: 99.9% for the isolation pool (monthly)
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms (measured at token level from edge)
- Support: 24x7 pager for Sev1 during pilot, escalation path to eng on-call

Next steps / asks for you
1) Confirm the baseline GPU count (8) and peak burst window.
2) Procurement timeline and PO cadence (approx date).
3) Share any SOX/SOC2 evidence requirements we should attach to the SOW.

Next steps from us
- I attached a short onramp MOP & the rough SLA draft (aurelia-mop-outline.pdf, sla-draft-aurelia.docx).
- We’ll put together a cost sketch (TCO for baseline + burst) and a one-page mutual action plan by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30-min call if you want to walk the numbers live.

Best,
Diego Fernández
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Cc: Aurelia Health Procurement <procurement@aurelia.health>
Date: 2027-04-04T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia onramp: notes + baseline ask

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Baseline count: 8 GPUs looks right for the initial estimate; can you include a sensitivity table showing throughput vs GPU count? CFO wants a clear breakpoint for commit levels.
- Burst: confirmed 06:00–10:00 PT is the high window; we may need occasional weekend bursts (approx 1–2x/month) — please add a burst credit line item.
- Security evidence: procurement needs SOC2 Type II and an HSM/KMS diagram. If you can point us to the standard packages you provide, procurement can validate faster.

Procurement timeline: we are targeting a signed PO by 2027-05-10 assuming legal + security review move at normal pace. If you can give a rough price for baseline + estimated monthly burst credits by tomorrow that will help.

On the pilot: we prefer the pilot to include a short spike test during the second week so we can validate autoscaling and fallback behavior.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Hargrove
Head of Infrastructure — Aurelia Health

- Monica: can you draft a pricing sketch for 8-GPU reserved baseline + burst credits to 24 GPUs (include a sensitivity table for 6/8/12/24), and a simple monthly cost line for 2 pilot weeks? Attach to the HubSpot deal above.
- Ben: can you pull the standard SOC2 Type II evidence bundle and the KMS/HSM diagram (we have a redacted version we share for RFPs) and upload to the Drive link. Procurement specifically asked for HSM integration notes and audit log retention (90/365 day options).

I attached the MOP and SLA draft again for reference. I’ll prepare the mutual action plan and a proposed pilot runbook (including the scheduled spike test) and send by tomorrow EOD so procurement has something to attach to the PO.

--
Diego
